source.title: Rethinking Generalization in Reasoning SFT: A Conditional Analysis on Optimization, Data, and Model Capability
source.authors: Qi-Han Ren; Peng Wang; Rui-Kun Cai; Shuai Shao; Da-Di Guo; Yue-Jin Xie; Ya-Fu Li; Quan-Shi Zhang; Xia Hu; Jing Shao; Dong-Rui Liu

record.file_problem: The supplied text includes the main paper and appendices. Some results are presented only in figures, but the text describes their trends.
record.tranche_reason: Tests reasoning-SFT generalization in pretrained language models and additional conditions, a setting not covered by the listed claim versions. The results concern in-domain benchmark transfer and cross-domain transfer, not random-label memorization or same-distribution generalization as defined by those versions.
record.gate_note: The paper reports many SFT benchmark results that bear on generalization in the claim's broader subject area, but none tests the specific behaviors in V1–V8. Its cross-domain results are outside the claim's stated scope; extracted results are recorded under fits_no_version. Cited prior-work results are not rows. Figure-only curves are described qualitatively where the text states the trend.
record.test_reason: The study measures benchmark transfer after reasoning SFT, not any behavior specified by V1–V8. Model-size comparisons do not establish interpolation thresholds; all SFT runs use AdamW without an SGD comparison; and Table 1 changes dataset size or epoch count alongside batch size, preventing a fixed-data, fixed-epoch batch-size test.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the authors' conclusion: reasoning-SFT transfer depends on optimization, data quality and structure, and base-model capability, while reasoning gains can accompany safety degradation. Their claim of marginal or negative gains on every benchmark for Qwen3-1.7B is inconsistent with Table 19. Their proposed procedural explanation is an interpretation supported by behavioral proxies, not an established internal mechanism.
record.recipe_differences: Reasoning SFT with long chain-of-thought supervision on pretrained language models, evaluated across benchmark domains; it does not reproduce random-label fitting or measure the specific phenomena in V1–V8.
record.method_sensitivity: Training duration and schedule, learning rate, data quality and structure, base-model capability, training domain, and benchmark domain change reported outcomes.

fits_no_version.finding: One-epoch math SFT improves math accuracy but reduces instruction-following accuracy; extended default training yields recovery and gains on several cross-domain benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Cross-domain transfer from long-CoT SFT can depend on optimization duration and exhibit early degradation followed by recovery.

fits_no_version.finding: At 640 updates and batch size 32, eight passes over 2.5k examples outperform one pass over 20k examples on AIME24 and LiveCodeBench, though Table 1 shows an exception on HaluEval.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Repeated exposure can outperform one-pass coverage at matched update budgets in reasoning SFT, with benchmark-dependent benefits.

fits_no_version.finding: High learning rate, constant learning rate, and extended training together produce late-stage declines on several reasoning and instruction-following benchmarks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-SFT performance can deteriorate under aggressive optimization schedules.

fits_no_version.finding: Transfer varies with supervision and base model: Qwen3-14B LiveCodeBench accuracy reaches 55.1% with Math-CoT, 40.3% with Math-NoCoT, 20.4% with NuminaMath, and 43.8% with Countdown-CoT. The 1.7B model has mixed benchmark outcomes rather than uniformly negligible gains.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Reasoning-SFT transfer depends on training-data composition and base-model capability, with substantial variation across evaluation tasks.

fits_no_version.finding: Qwen3-14B attack success rises from 20.0% at baseline to 53.7% after Math-CoT SFT, versus 23.3% after matched Math-NoCoT SFT.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Long-CoT reasoning SFT can weaken safety more than matched supervision without the thinking trace.

record.peer_reviewed: Published as a conference paper at COLM 2026
record.problems: The authors note that math reasoning is the primary controlled training domain, the study does not include substantially larger dense models or mixture-of-experts architectures, it lacks a full factorial analysis of interaction effects, and trace-level analyses use rule-based detectors. Several training-trajectory results are figure-only and lack exact values in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Many separately reported checkpoint, model-family, benchmark, data, and schedule values are present in Appendix C and D and exceed the useful row budget if exhaustively included. The selected rows retain illustrative numerical comparisons for short versus extended training, repeated exposure, data variants, model capability, aggressive schedules, and the safety comparison. Figure-only trajectories not transcribed as exact numbers are summarized only where the text explicitly describes them.

untested.parts: Coexistence of random-label fitting and natural-label generalization under the same architecture and training recipe; chance performance on held-out random labels.
Test error as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or convolution-derived initialization.
Adaptive versus SGD-based optimization under limited or broader tuning, including switching optimizers and decoupled weight decay comparisons.
Batch-size effects with dataset and epoch budget held fixed, and recipes that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout effects, small-training-set exceptions, underfitting from excessive dropout, and removal with weight decay under augmentation.
Magnitude-aware sharpness, its association with train-test gaps, and comparisons against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples and retraining.

record.verdict_notes: T3 is inappropriate because a new setting must still test a listed version. Citing the AdamW original and using AdamW do not test V4. All row states remain cannot_determine relative to V1–V8 because their measures do not establish those effects; this does not imply their benchmark values are unreadable.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out natural-label performance under the same architecture and recipe.
Width sweeps past the interpolation threshold in one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and local connectivity.
Adaptive versus non-adaptive optimizers under the specified tuning regimes and benchmarks.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and adaptive recipes.
Dropout effects in the specified classifier and training-set regimes.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and its relation to train-test gaps.
Removing the most memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
